title: House Shadash
content:
**House Shadash** is an ancient and insular house of obscure origin, seated on the island of [[Thorsef]], the largest of a small
archipelago a day's sailing from [[Verithold]]. Known for their dark grey eyes, their quiet apartness, and the persistent — if largely
unfounded — suspicion that they harbour old secrets.

## History

**Founded:** Unknown — predates reliable record
**Seat:** [[Thorsef]] (island)
**Sigil:** Unknown
**Words:** *"Not All That Fades Is Lost"*
**Sworn to:** [[House Wilfrey of Fourhearth]]

The origins of House Shadash are poorly documented. They claim no founding hero, no royal grant, no origin story of the kind other
houses recite with pride. They were simply already on Thorsef when the records began.

## Holdings and Influence

The Shadash hold [[Thorsef]], a sparsely populated mountain island, and claim authority over the surrounding archipelago collectively
known as the Sefs. These include [[Nelsef]], seat of a lesser branch of the house, and three unsettled islands: [[Asef]], [[Pitsef]],
and [[Vinsef]], each home to unusual flora and fauna found nowhere on the mainland.

The Shadash attend court infrequently and show minimal interest in political manoeuvring. Their power, such as it is, lies in longevity
and self-sufficiency — they have outlasted families far more ambitious than themselves.

## The Minor Branch

A lesser branch of the house occupies the smaller island of [[Nelsef]]. More reclusive than the main house, they practise strict
endogamy — marriage exclusively within the bloodline — insisting the old blood must remain undiluted. Their practices are incestuous by
the standards of [[Crown of Estargenn|Estargenn]] law. They maintain them regardless, regarding such prohibitions as modern inventions
with no authority over far older obligations.

## Relations

**Sworn to:** [[House Wilfrey of Fourhearth]]
**Allies:** None formally declared

**Rivals:** None formally declared

The Shadash maintain no open feuds and pursue no alliances. Other houses regard them with a mixture of curiosity and wariness — a
wariness sharpened by the archipelago's proximity to [[Verithold]], seat of all recorded knowledge in Estargenn. That a family so
private should dwell within sight of the realm's greatest repository of knowledge strikes many as either deeply ironic or deeply
suspicious.

## The Grey Eyes

All Shadash of the main line share a distinctive deep grey eye colour — dark as wet slate, unsettling in low light. The trait breeds
true even through mixed parentage. Folk ascribe various superstitions to the eyes. The Shadash consider them unremarkable.

## Current Status

House Shadash endures on Thorsef, as it always has — quietly, apart, and largely misunderstood. The wider community whispers that they
keep secrets. The Shadash, if asked, would not understand the question.

title: The Sefs
subtitle: The Shadash Archipelago
content:
**The Sefs** is the common name for a small archipelago of five islands, a day's sailing from [[Verithold]]. The seat of [[House
Shadash]], the chain is home to unusual flora and fauna found nowhere on the mainland.

## The Islands

| Island | Character |
|--------|-----------|
| [[Thorsef]] | Mountain island. Largest of the chain. Main Shadash seat |
| [[Nelsef]] | Smaller, harder. Seat of the Shadash minor branch |
| [[Asef]] | Bare, wind-scoured, stripped to essentials |
| [[Pitsef]] | Low-lying, sudden deep water, tidal pools — things surface that shouldn't |
| [[Vinsef]] | Bleached dead trees, minimal life — what survives is tough and strange |

Only Thorsef and Nelsef are settled. The remaining three are unsettled but claimed by the Shadash.

## The Name

Outsiders coined "the Sefs" by noticing the shared suffix across all five island names. They regard it as a local naming convention.
None have investigated further.

## Proximity to Verithold

The chain lies within sight of [[Verithold]], seat of all recorded knowledge in [[Crown of Estargenn|Estargenn]]. That a family so
private should dwell so close to the realm's greatest repository of knowledge strikes many as either deeply ironic or deeply suspicious.
The Shadash have no known formal relationship with the Veritists.

title: Thorsef
subtitle: Seat of House Shadash
content:
**Thorsef** is a sparsely populated mountain island, the largest of [[the Sefs]] archipelago, and the ancestral seat of [[House
Shadash]]. A day's sailing from [[Verithold]], the island is dominated by a central mountain and ringed by rocky coastline.

## Character

Thorsef is austere rather than bleak — a place of stone, wind, and long views. The mountain gives the island a sense of weight and
permanence. The Shadash have lived here since before reliable records began, and the island feels shaped by that long occupation in ways
that are difficult to articulate but immediately felt by visitors.

## The Waking Dream

The founding story of Thorsef holds that a waking man dreamed the island before he saw it — that it came into his waking light, tall and
present. Whether the Shadash still tell this story fully, or only in fragments, varies by generation.

## Holdings

The Shadash maintain their seat on Thorsef and claim authority over the surrounding archipelago. The island supports a small,
self-sufficient population. Visitors are infrequent and not especially encouraged.

## See Also
- [[House Shadash]]: The ancient house that holds this island
- [[The Sefs]]: The archipelago of which Thorsef is the largest
- [[Nelsef]]: Seat of the Shadash minor branch

title: Nelsef
subtitle: Seat of the Shadmoor Cadet Branch
content:
**Nelsef** is a small island in [[the Sefs]] archipelago, seat of the lesser branch of [[House Shadash]]; [[House Shadmoor]]. Smaller and harder than [[Thorsef]], it is home to the most reclusive members of an already reclusive family.

## The Minor Branch

The Shadmoor cadet branch who occupy Nelsef practise strict endogamy — marriage exclusively within the bloodline — driven by a conviction that the "old blood" must remain undiluted. They view
intermarriage with the wider population not merely as undesirable but as a form of erasure: each generation of mixed blood is, to them, another step toward forgetting what they are.

Their practices are incestuous by the standards of [[Crown of Estargenn|Estargenn]] law. They maintain them regardless, regarding such prohibitions as modern inventions with no authority
over obligations far older than any charter or crown.

## Character

Where [[Thorsef]] is austere, Nelsef is severe. The island is smaller, the coastline sharper, the settlement more fortress than village. Contact with the main house on Thorsef is maintained but not frequent. Contact with the wider world is rarer still.

## See Also
- [[House Shadash]]: The main house on Thorsef
- [[House Shadmoor]]: Cadet branch on Nelsef
- [[The Old Blood]]: What the minor branch seeks to preserve
- [[The Sefs]]: The archipelago

title: Asef
subtitle: The Bare Island
content:
**Asef** is one of three unsettled islands in [[the Sefs]] archipelago, claimed by [[House Shadash]] but uninhabited. The smallest and most exposed of the chain, Asef is bare and
wind-scoured — stripped to essentials by centuries of unbroken weather.

## Character

There is almost nothing on Asef. No trees, no shelter, no fresh water worth mentioning. What remains is rock, wind, and the sea. The island has the quality of something that has been
reduced to its fundamental elements — everything unnecessary has been taken away, and what persists does so because it cannot be removed.

## See Also
- [[The Sefs]]: The archipelago
- [[House Shadash]]: Claimants of the island

title: Pitsef
subtitle: The Deep Island
content:
**Pitsef** is one of three unsettled islands in [[the Sefs]] archipelago, claimed by [[House Shadash]] but uninhabited. Low-lying and unremarkable from a distance, the island is defined
by what lies beneath its surface.

## Character

Pitsef sits low in the water. Its coastline is riddled with tidal pools of unusual depth — sudden drops where the sea floor falls away without warning. Things surface in these pools that
have no business being in shallow water: deep-sea creatures, strange shells, objects tumbled smooth by currents that run far below.

The island unsettles visitors. Not because anything happens there, but because the ground feels thin — as though the real island is somewhere beneath, and what you're standing on is
merely its lid.

## See Also
- [[The Sefs]]: The archipelago
- [[House Shadash]]: Claimants of the island

title: Vinsef
subtitle: The Withered Island
content:
**Vinsef** is one of three unsettled islands in [[the Sefs]] archipelago, claimed by [[House Shadash]] but uninhabited. The outermost island of the chain, Vinsef is a place where things
have stopped growing but not quite finished dying.

## Character

The island is covered in bleached dead trees — pale trunks standing like bones against the sky, leafless but refusing to fall. The soil supports almost nothing. What survives on Vinsef is
tough and strange: lichens of unusual colour, insects found nowhere else, a few species of bird that nest in the dead wood and seem to thrive on whatever the island provides.

The effect is eerie without being hostile. Vinsef is not a threatening place — it is simply a place where the ordinary rules of growth and decay seem to have been suspended, leaving
everything in a state of permanent, quiet endurance.

## See Also
- [[The Sefs]]: The archipelago
- [[House Shadash]]: Claimants of the island

title: The Old Blood
subtitle: Bloodline Beyond Memory
content:
**The Old Blood** is a phrase used — by others more than by the Shadash themselves — to describe the quality that sets [[House Shadash]] apart. It implies lineage stretching back beyond
the memory of current institutions, bloodline connections to something prior to the established order.

## Common Understanding

Most in [[Crown of Estargenn|Estargenn]] interpret "old blood" in purely genealogical terms: the Shadash are an ancient family, perhaps one of the oldest in the region, and their
strangeness is simply the eccentricity of an old line that hasn't refreshed itself enough. This is not wrong — it is just vastly incomplete.

## Visible Markers

The most recognisable marker of the old blood is [[The Grey Eyes]] — a distinctive deep grey eye colour shared by all Shadash of the main line. The trait breeds remarkably true, even
through mixed parentage.

## House Shadmoor, the insular cadet branch

The lesser branch of House Shadash on [[Nelsef]] practises strict endogamy in an effort to preserve the old blood undiluted. They view intermarriage as a form of erasure — each generation
of mixed blood another step toward forgetting. Their commitment to preservation carries costs that grow more visible with each generation.

## See Also
- [[House Shadmoor]]: Cadet branch that worships old blood purity 
- [[House Shadash]]: The family that carries the old blood
- [[The Grey Eyes]]: The most visible marker
- [[Nelsef]]: Where the minor branch preserves the bloodline

title: The Grey Eyes
subtitle: Mark of House Shadash
content:
**The Grey Eyes** are the most immediately recognisable feature of Shadash blood — a distinctive deep grey eye colour, dark as wet slate or storm cloud. Not the pale grey common among
some northern folk, but something deeper, almost mineral.

## Appearance

In ordinary light, the eyes are merely unusual. In certain conditions — low light, candlelight, direct attention — they can be genuinely unsettling. There is a quality of *depth* to them
that makes people feel observed rather than merely looked at. This is not supernatural (as far as anyone knows). It is simply what Shadash eyes look like.

## Heritability

The trait breeds remarkably true. Even Shadash with mixed parentage frequently show the grey, though sometimes lighter or with flecks of the other parent's colour. Among the main line,
the eyes are uniformly dark grey with very little variation.

## Folk Beliefs

The surrounding population has developed various superstitions:
- That the Shadash can see in the dark (unsubstantiated but persistent)
- That meeting a Shadash's gaze brings ill luck (widely dismissed but still avoided by the superstitious)
- That the grey comes from "old blood" that hasn't mixed enough with common stock
- That the eyes mark them as touched by something — nobody agrees on what

The Shadash themselves consider their eyes unremarkable. It is simply what eyes look like in their family. The fact that others find them notable is, to the Shadash, yet another example
of the wider world's tendency to make something strange out of something ordinary.

## See Also
- [[House Shadash]]: The family that carries the trait
- [[The Old Blood]]: The lineage that produces it
